page.layout: One printed page. Running head "EMBLEMA" centred above the title. Page number 170 at top left. Title block in large italic capitals with a line in italic below, centred. Below it a woodcut emblem filling the middle of the page (no text inside it). Below the woodcut, a four-line verse set centred in italic. A catchword-like signature "De" at lower right, below the verse.

main_text.head: VIA LATA QVÆ DVCIT ad inferos.
main_text.p:
Fige pedem, properare caue, non est via recta,
Ad cælum haud præsens ingredieris iter!
Horrida crudelis trahit hic ad tartara saltus,
Ergo gratum reuoca, quæso, pedemq; refer.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a procession of people in early modern dress, led by a skeleton and a winged devil, walking down a path toward a gaping hell-mouth at lower right; a skeleton with a torch appears at the top right. The title line "ad inferos" is set in smaller italic beneath "VIA LATA QVÆ DVCIT". The "De" at lower right is a catchword or signature mark, possibly cut off. Verse lines are set with the same italic type; the verse is centred, not indented as a paragraph.
